Create a Volcano Plot

Source: R/ggvolc.R
ggvolc.Rd

This function creates a volcano plot using ggplot2 based on provided datasets. It is particularly useful for visualizing differential gene expression data.

Usage

ggvolc(
  data1,
  data2 = NULL,
  size_var = NULL,
  p_value = 0.05,
  fc = 1,
  sig_col = c("padj", "pvalue"),
  label_top = NULL,
  label_dir = c("both", "up", "down", "each"),
  title = NULL,
  interactive = FALSE,
  palette = "default",
  not_sig_color = NULL,
  down_reg_color = NULL,
  up_reg_color = NULL,
  add_seg = FALSE,
  show_counts = FALSE,
  highlight = NULL,
  highlight_colors = NULL,
  facet_scales = c("free_y", "fixed", "free_x", "free"),
  coef = NULL
)

Arguments

data1

The DE results to plot: a data frame, or a DESeq2 (DESeqResults, DESeqDataSet), edgeR (TopTags, DGELRT, DGEExact) or limma (MArrayLM) object. Gene identifiers can live in a genes column or in the row names. To compare contrasts, pass a named list of results, e.g. list("Day 1" = res1, "Day 7" = res7): each becomes a panel on shared axes, and label_top and show_counts work per panel.

data2

Genes to highlight and label: a data frame or DE object (same auto-detection as data1), or simply a character vector of gene names. With a list in data1, the genes are highlighted in every panel. Default is NULL.

size_var

Variable for determining the size of points. Options are "log2FoldChange" and "pvalue". Default is NULL (fixed size).

p_value

Threshold for statistical significance. Default is 0.05.

fc

Fold change threshold for determining upregulated or downregulated genes. Default is 1.

sig_col

Column used to call significance and to build the y-axis. Either "padj" (the adjusted p-value / FDR, the default and the recommended cutoff for calling hits in most DE workflows) or "pvalue" (the raw p-value). The y-axis and the significance segment follow this choice, so the plot stays internally consistent. When the default "padj" is used but the data has no adjusted-p column, ggvolc falls back to the raw p-value.

label_top

Optional integer. When supplied, the label_top most significant genes (smallest sig_col, among significant genes) are highlighted and labelled automatically, without building a separate data2. Combined with data2 if both are given. Default NULL.

label_dir

Direction to draw the label_top genes from. One of "both" (top N over all significant genes, the default), "up" (top N upregulated), "down" (top N downregulated), or "each" (top N upregulated and top N downregulated, i.e. up to 2N labels). Ignored when label_top is NULL.

title

Plot title. Default NULL (no title).

interactive

Logical. If TRUE, returns an interactive ggiraph girafe widget where hovering a point reveals the gene name and its statistics. Requires the optional ggiraph package. Default FALSE.

palette

Colors for the plot: a preset name (see ggvolc_palettes), such as "default", "okabe_ito" (colorblind-safe), or one of the ltc-derived presets, or a named vector such as c(down = "navy", up = "firebrick").

not_sig_color, down_reg_color, up_reg_color

Colors for non-significant, downregulated, and upregulated genes. When given, they override the matching color from palette. Default NULL.

add_seg

Logical. If TRUE, dashed lines will be added to the plot indicating the p-value and fold change thresholds. Default is FALSE.

show_counts

Logical. If TRUE, the number of significantly down- and upregulated genes is printed in the top corners of the plot (of each panel when comparing contrasts). Default FALSE.

highlight

Optional named list of gene sets to color, e.g. list(Ribosome = c("RPL3", "RPS2"), Glycolysis = c("PFK1", "PYK1")). Genes in a set are drawn in the set's color, whatever their significance, and each set gets a legend entry. A gene in several sets takes the first.

highlight_colors

Optional colors for the highlight sets, in order or named by set. Defaults to colorblind-friendly Okabe-Ito hues.

facet_scales

When comparing contrasts, which axes each panel may set for itself. The default "free_y" keeps the fold-change (x) axis shared, so effect sizes stay comparable, while each panel uses its full height for significance, so a weaker contrast is not squashed by a stronger one. Use "fixed" to share both axes, or "free_x" / "free".

coef

For a multi-coefficient limma fit, the coefficient to plot; for a DESeqDataSet, the result name. See de_table.

Value

A ggplot2 object displaying the volcano plot, or, when interactive = TRUE, a ggiraph girafe widget.

Details

You can pass the result objects of DESeq2, edgeR, and limma directly (see de_table), or a data frame. Column names from all three pipelines are detected and mapped automatically.

Examples

# Load example datasets included in the package
data(all_genes)
data(attention_genes)

# Create a basic volcano plot with default settings
# Points are colored by significance (p < 0.05, |log2FC| > 1)
ggvolc(all_genes)


# Highlight specific genes of interest with labels
# These genes are shown with black borders and gene names
ggvolc(all_genes, attention_genes)


# \donttest{
# Add dashed lines to indicate significance thresholds
ggvolc(all_genes, attention_genes, add_seg = TRUE)


# Significance is called on the adjusted p-value (FDR) by default;
# use the raw p-value instead with:
ggvolc(all_genes, sig_col = "pvalue")


# Automatically label the 10 most significant genes
ggvolc(all_genes, label_top = 10)


# Label the top 10 upregulated genes only
ggvolc(all_genes, label_top = 10, label_dir = "up")


# Label the top 8 of each direction (up to 16 labels)
ggvolc(all_genes, label_top = 8, label_dir = "each")


# Give the plot a title
ggvolc(all_genes, title = "Treated vs. control")


# Show how many genes go up and down
ggvolc(all_genes, show_counts = TRUE)


# Color gene sets, e.g. a pathway
ggvolc(all_genes, highlight = list(Set_A = all_genes$genes[1:15],
                                   Set_B = all_genes$genes[100:130]))


# Compare contrasts side by side: a real stress time course
ggvolc(stress_timecourse, label_top = 5, show_counts = TRUE)
#> ggvolc: left out 384 gene(s) with NA padj or log2FoldChange (e.g. genes DESeq2 filtered as low-count or outliers).


# Share the y-axis too, to compare significance between panels
ggvolc(stress_timecourse, label_top = 5, facet_scales = "fixed")
#> ggvolc: left out 384 gene(s) with NA padj or log2FoldChange (e.g. genes DESeq2 filtered as low-count or outliers).


# Colorblind-safe colors, or any preset from ggvolc_palettes()
ggvolc(all_genes, label_top = 10, palette = "okabe_ito")


# Customize colors for up- and down-regulated genes
ggvolc(all_genes, attention_genes,
       up_reg_color = "#E63946",
       down_reg_color = "#457B9D")


# Scale point size by p-value instead of default
ggvolc(all_genes, attention_genes, size_var = "pvalue")


# Adjust significance thresholds (p-value and fold change)
ggvolc(all_genes, p_value = 0.01, fc = 2)


# edgeR-style input works directly
edger_df <- data.frame(
  genes = paste0("gene", 1:50),
  logFC = rnorm(50, 0, 2),
  logCPM = runif(50, 5, 15),
  PValue = 10^-runif(50, 0, 6),
  FDR = 10^-runif(50, 0, 5)
)
ggvolc(edger_df)


# limma-style input works too
limma_df <- data.frame(
  genes = paste0("gene", 1:50),
  logFC = rnorm(50, 0, 2),
  AveExpr = runif(50, 5, 15),
  t = rnorm(50),
  P.Value = 10^-runif(50, 0, 6),
  adj.P.Val = 10^-runif(50, 0, 5)
)
ggvolc(limma_df)


# }

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# DE objects work directly, no conversion needed
ggvolc(DESeq2::results(dds))
ggvolc(edgeR::glmQLFTest(qlf_fit, coef = 2))
ggvolc(limma::eBayes(limma_fit), coef = "treatment")

# Interactive volcano (requires the ggiraph package): hover a point to
# see the gene name and its statistics
ggvolc(all_genes, attention_genes, interactive = TRUE)
} # }
